name: ctpop-islet-parameterization
title: CTpop -> Topp2000 Islet Parameterization — Beta-Cell Composition Shifts the Glucose Setpoint
question:
Does binding HRA CTpop islet cell-type composition to the Topp2000
beta-cell-mass model (BIOMD0000000341) change the predicted glucose
regulation -- realizing the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization vision
Katy Boerner / Peter Hunter / SPARC describe, for the pancreatic islet FTU
`ftu-model-coverage` already found covered?

study_card.goal: Map a documented HRA-aligned islet beta-cell fraction onto the Topp2000 model's initial beta-cell mass (B), and run healthy (54% beta) vs beta-depleted (30% beta, the T2D-relevant loss) scenarios to see whether the composition shift changes the model's predicted glucose trajectory.
study_card.mechanism: CtpopIsletParameterizationStep.update -> compare_islet_compositions((0.54, 0.30)) -> per fraction: _fetch_topp_sbml(BIOMD0000000341) via the `biomodels` package -> _default_b_ref_from_sbml reads the model's own default initial B (37) out of the SBML -> beta_fraction_to_beta_mass(beta_fraction, b_ref) = b_ref * beta_fraction / 0.54 -> pbg_tellurium.TelluriumProcess loaded on the SBML with species_overrides={'B': b_init} -> one continuous roadrunner.simulate(0, 4000, 200) call over the model's DAYS timescale -> {time, B, G, I} trajectory -> RAMEmitter.
study_card.expected_result: The healthy islet (54% beta, b_init=37=b_ref) settles near the model's physiological fixed point (G ~100 mg/dL); the beta-depleted islet (30% beta, b_init~20.6) crosses the model's bifurcation into its pathological fixed point (G ~600 mg/dL, B and I collapsing toward 0) -- a real, mechanistically-driven glucose-regulation consequence of the composition shift, not a cosmetic one.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is proportional initial-mass rescaling (B_init = b_ref * beta_fraction / 0.54) a defensible way to bind a CTpop cell-type fraction to this model, or should alpha/delta fractions also enter via separate parameters (e.g. glucagon secretion, insulin-secretion modulation) rather than folding everything into B alone?

biological_summary:
`ftu-model-coverage` identified the pancreatic islet as an HRA functional
tissue unit already covered by curated BioModels (Topp2000, Jiang2007,
Bertram2007) and stubbed (via `ctpop_parameter_stub`) the islet's
beta/alpha/delta cell types (CL:0000169/0171/0173) as candidate CTpop
(Cell Type Populations, Bueckle 2026) parameterization targets, without
binding any real count. This study takes that next step for Topp2000
(BIOMD0000000341, Topp et al. 2000 J Theor Biol): it binds a documented
HRA-aligned islet beta-cell-fraction (a live CTpop API pull is not
publicly exposed as JSON as of this writing, so this study uses
documented literature/HRA-ASCT+B composition values instead, cited in
`ISLET_COMPOSITION` -- beta 54%, alpha 34%, delta 10%, PP/epsilon ~2%,
per Cabrera et al. 2006 PNAS and Brissova et al. 2005) onto the Topp
model's initial beta-cell mass B, via
`B_init = b_ref * (beta_fraction / 0.54)` where `b_ref` (37, the model's
own SBML-declared default initial B) is read out of the model, not
hardcoded. The Topp model is deliberately built to operate on a DAYS
timescale (beta-cell-mass turnover is slow relative to glucose/insulin
kinetics), so this study runs it out to 4,000 model-time-units (~11
years) -- long enough for the model's slow beta-cell-mass compartment to
reach a new steady state. Running both a healthy islet (54% beta,
b_init=37, reproducing the model's own default) and a beta-depleted
islet (30% beta, the T2D-relevant beta-cell loss, b_init~20.6) shows the
composition binding lands on a real mechanistic knife-edge in this model:
the healthy islet settles at the model's physiological fixed point
(glucose ~100 mg/dL, a normal fasting-range value), while the
beta-depleted islet crosses Topp2000's bifurcation into the pathological
fixed point (glucose ~600 mg/dL, severe hyperglycemia, with beta-cell
mass and insulin both collapsing toward zero) -- exactly the "mild vs.
extreme beta-cell loss" bifurcation behavior the original Topp et al.
2000 paper describes as its central diabetes-progression finding. So
binding CTpop composition to this model doesn't just nudge a number, it
flips which of the model's two stable regimes the trajectory lands in.
readouts: runs.<scenario>.b_init / b_ref / beta_fraction (the CTpop-fraction -> beta-cell-mass binding)
reference_beta_fraction (0.54, the healthy-reference the binding scales against)

report.title: CTpop -> Topp2000 Islet Parameterization — Beta-Depleted Islet Crosses the Model's Diabetes Bifurcation
report.objective:
Does binding HRA CTpop islet cell-type composition to the Topp2000
beta-cell-mass model change its predicted glucose regulation?
report.conclusion:
Yes, decisively. Binding the documented healthy islet composition
(54% beta) reproduces the Topp2000 model's own default initial
beta-cell mass (b_ref=37) exactly and the model settles at its
physiological fixed point: glucose falls from an initial 250 to
~100.0 mg/dL over 4,000 model-days, beta-cell mass grows from 37 to
~300, insulin rises from 2.8 to ~10.0. Binding the T2D-relevant
beta-depleted composition (30% beta, the documented beta-cell loss)
scales the initial mass down to ~20.56 (37 * 0.30/0.54) and the
SAME model, run identically, crosses Topp2000's beta-cell-mass
bifurcation into its pathological fixed point: glucose rises to
~600.0 mg/dL (severe hyperglycemia) while beta-cell mass and insulin
both collapse toward 0. This mechanistically links a real, cited
HRA-aligned cell-type-composition difference to a qualitatively
different physiological regime in a real, published beta-cell-mass
model -- not just a small parameter perturbation, but a flip between
the model's two documented stable states (Topp et al. 2000's own
central finding about mild vs. extreme beta-cell loss).
report.caveat:
`ISLET_COMPOSITION` is documented literature/HRA-ASCT+B composition
(Cabrera et al. 2006 PNAS; Brissova et al. 2005), not a live HRA CTpop
API pull for a specific RUI-registered tissue block -- a live query
would give a real measured composition instead of a population-average
literature value, and a live CTpop endpoint is not (as of this writing)
publicly exposed as JSON. The binding is initial-mass-only: only the
beta fraction enters the model (via B_init), and only as an initial
condition, not a rate parameter -- alpha/delta fractions are identified
(`ISLET_COMPOSITION`) but not bound to any Topp2000 parameter (e.g.
glucagon secretion isn't in this model at all). So
`pipeline_gate.gate_evaluator.result` is `needs_calibration`.

embed_visualizations.name: Glucose vs islet composition
embed_visualizations.description: Topp2000 glucose G(t) over 4,000 model-days: healthy islet (54% beta) settles at ~100 mg/dL (physiological); beta-depleted islet (30% beta, the T2D-relevant beta-cell loss) crosses the model's bifurcation to ~600 mg/dL (pathological hyperglycemia), beta-cell mass and insulin collapsing toward 0.

findings.statement:
Binding the documented healthy islet composition (54% beta) to
Topp2000's initial beta-cell mass reproduces the model's own default
(b_ref=37) and the model settles at its physiological fixed point
(glucose ~100 mg/dL over 4,000 model-days). Binding the documented
T2D-relevant beta-depleted composition (30% beta) scales the initial
mass down to ~20.56 and the identical model crosses Topp2000's
beta-cell-mass bifurcation into its pathological fixed point (glucose
~600 mg/dL, beta-cell mass and insulin collapsing toward 0) -- the
CTpop composition mechanistically shifts which of the model's two
stable regimes the glucose trajectory lands in, not merely its
numeric value.

evidence.summary: healthy (beta=0.54, b_init=37=b_ref): G 250->100.0, B 37->300.0, I 2.8->10.0 (physiological fixed point). beta_depleted (beta=0.30, b_init=20.56): G 250->600.0, B 20.56->~0, I 2.8->~0 (pathological fixed point) -- same model, same 4,000-model-day horizon, differing only in the CTpop-composition-bound initial beta-cell mass.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline ctpop-islet-parameterization composite (CtpopIsletParameterizationStep -> compare_islet_compositions) completed without error for both scenarios, emitting non-empty runs.healthy / runs.beta_depleted trajectories with real BioModels-fetched, tellurium-solved numbers.

biological_validation.basis: ISLET_COMPOSITION is documented literature/HRA-ASCT+B composition (Cabrera 2006 PNAS; Brissova 2005), not a live HRA CTpop API pull, and the binding is initial-mass-only (alpha/delta fractions identified but not bound to a model parameter), so gated needs_calibration rather than passed -- but the underlying model (BIOMD0000000341) is real and the binding (B_init = b_ref * beta_fraction / 0.54, b_ref read from the SBML) is a defensible, documented, non-hardcoded parameterization.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 directly answers the study question -- yes, binding CTpop islet composition to Topp2000 changes the predicted glucose regulation, and dramatically: it flips which of the model's two stable fixed points (physiological vs. pathological/diabetic) the trajectory settles into, realizing the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization vision for a real, covered FTU model rather than merely stubbing which parameters would be involved.

limitations: `ISLET_COMPOSITION` is documented literature/HRA-ASCT+B composition (Cabrera et al. 2006 PNAS; Brissova et al. 2005), not a live HRA CTpop API pull for a specific RUI-registered tissue block -- a live CTpop endpoint is not (as of this writing) publicly exposed as JSON.

Binding is initial-mass only: only the beta-cell fraction enters the Topp2000 model, and only as the initial condition for B, not as a rate/kinetic parameter -- alpha and delta fractions are identified (`ISLET_COMPOSITION`) but not bound to any Topp2000 parameter (the model has no glucagon/somatostatin compartment to bind them to).

The 30% beta-depleted scenario is a single illustrative T2D-relevant composition point, not a distribution over real measured islets -- the exact glucose/insulin/beta-mass endpoints (600 / ~0 / ~0) are specific to this one fraction and this one model's parameterization, not a general dose-response curve.

resolved_uncertainties: CTpop islet composition, bound as an initial-condition parameter (beta-cell mass), does mechanistically change Topp2000's predicted glucose regulation -- realizing (for one covered FTU model and one composition-to-parameter binding) the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization vision `ftu-model-coverage`'s `ctpop_parameter_stub` only stubbed.

The composition shift from healthy (54% beta) to T2D-relevant beta-depleted (30% beta) composition is large enough, in this model's parameterization, to cross a real bifurcation between the model's physiological and pathological fixed points -- not just perturb a number within one regime.
remaining_uncertainties: Does a LIVE HRA CTpop count (for a specific RUI-registered islet tissue block) differ materially from the documented literature-average composition used here, and if so, in which direction?

Should alpha/delta cell fractions bind to separate Topp2000-family or extended-model parameters (e.g. a glucagon-secretion term), rather than folding all islet composition information into the single beta-cell-mass initial condition?

followup_study_proposals.title: Bind a LIVE HRA CTpop islet cell count (not documented literature values) to Topp2000
followup_study_proposals.motivation: This study proves the mechanism (composition -> beta-cell mass -> glucose regime) using documented literature composition; a live per-tissue-block CTpop count would let a specific RUI-registered islet be parameterized against its own measured composition rather than a population average.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: When/if a live HRA CTpop JSON endpoint becomes available for a RUI-registered pancreatic-islet tissue block, fetch its real beta/alpha/delta-cell counts, compute the beta fraction from the real counts (not the documented 0.54/0.34/0.10/0.02 split), and re-run `compare_islet_compositions` with that live fraction in place of the documented one.

followup_study_proposals.title: Bind alpha/delta CTpop fractions to per-cell-type Topp-family model parameters
followup_study_proposals.motivation: This study binds only the beta fraction (to initial beta-cell mass); a fuller CTpop -> model parameterization would also bind alpha/delta fractions to whichever islet-model parameters they mechanistically govern (e.g. a glucagon-secretion-capable extended model).
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Identify or build an islet model with explicit alpha/delta-cell-mediated terms (e.g. glucagon counter-regulation), and bind CTpop alpha/delta fractions to those terms alongside the existing beta -> B binding, then compare against the beta-only binding used here.
